text: Same rail, header, composer and Alephic Product palette in all three; only the transcript, the Terminal switch and subagents differ. Real turns from this session. Open a tile for full size; the sun icon toggles dark.

Wins when: you mostly read what the agent said. Tool runs collapse to one quiet line, the subagent is a live row where it was launched, and Terminal is a drawer (Ctrl+J), like T3 Code, Codex and Claude desktop.
Cost: least information at a glance. Seeing what ran means a click, and on a wide screen the 736px column leaves empty margins.
Wins when: you supervise. Times, per-turn tool counts and failures stay visible, running subagents sit in a strip that never scrolls away, and the terminal stays open beside the conversation.
Cost: busiest of the three; the split halves the reading width, and the chips read like a dashboard.
Wins when: you come back to a long session. Each turn is one object (prompt, work timeline, answer), old turns fold to a line, and a subagent nests as a child card under the step that launched it.
Cost: most chrome per turn; cards and shadows cost height, and Conversation/Terminal tabs keep the swap model instead of showing both.

My pick: A · Thread. Your complaint was that the transcript reads like a debug log; A is the quietest fix and matches the agent apps you already use. I'd borrow C's nested subagent steps into A's live row.
